symptoms: The plant begins to wilt starting at the leaf tips or where stems branch out.
Leaves turn yellow at the base before the whole plant wilts and dies.
When you cut a stem, you will see a brown ring inside.
When you cut a tuber in half, you will see black or brown rings.
Squeezing a cut tuber releases a thick white fluid.
Fluid may come out of the tuber eyes and cause soil to stick to them.
favourable_conditions: High temperature, soil moisture, and low pH favour the disease.
prevention: Use only tubers that are free from the pathogen.
Rotate your potato crops with wheat.
Apply lime to the soil to change the pH level.
practices: Remove and destroy any plants that show signs of wilting.
Disinfect your cutting knife with a bleach solution.
Monitor your fields regularly for signs of the disease.
Avoid moving soil or water from infected areas to healthy ones.
